slot.brief: Simplify a vector triple product a×(b×c) using the standard identity and evaluate a resulting dot/scalar quantity.

stem: Given $\vec a=\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$, $\vec b=2\hat i+\hat k$, $\vec c=\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$ and $\vec d=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$, find $[\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)]\cdot\vec d$.

verdicts.working: Using a×(b×c)=b(a·c)−c(a·b), we have a·c=−3, a·b=1, b·d=3, and c·d=2. Thus the expression is −3(3)−2=−11.

working:
$\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b(\vec a\cdot\vec c)-\vec c(\vec a\cdot\vec b)$
$\vec a\cdot\vec c=-3,\quad \vec a\cdot\vec b=1$
$\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=-3\vec b-\vec c=-7\hat i+\hat j-5\hat k$
$[\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)]\cdot\vec d=-7+1-5=-11$

Independent check: Using a×(b×c)=b(a·c)−c(a·b), we have a·c=−3, a·b=1, b·d=3, and c·d=2. Thus the expression is −3(3)−2=−11.
solution:
Using $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b(\vec a\cdot\vec c)-\vec c(\vec a\cdot\vec b)$, we have $\vec a\cdot\vec c=-3$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=1$, $\vec b\cdot\vec d=3$, and $\vec c\cdot\vec d=2$.
$$[\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)]\cdot\vec d=(-3)(3)-(1)(2)=-11$$
